subject: Proposed language: incident notification timelines & cooperation (DPA)
messages:
From: Jane Alvarez <j.alvarez@acme-corp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Incident notification timing and cooperation language for DPA

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our Legal team is asking us to confirm the breach notification window and scope of cooperation we can expect from Redwood in the event of a security incident that affects Acme customer data. The DPA we shared includes a 48-hour initial notification requirement and a clause requiring "reasonable cooperation" for remediation and root-cause analysis.

Two requests from Legal:
- Can Redwood confirm whether 48 hours is feasible for an initial notification that includes confirmed scope (affected systems/users) or whether that needs to be an "initial notice within 48 hours with follow-up as info becomes available"?
- Can we get concrete examples of what "reasonable cooperation" means operationally (e.g., technical point of contact, evidence access, joint communications, preservation of logs, timelines for deliverables)?

We'd like to avoid an open-ended obligation that could force production access or unrealistic timelines. If you could propose specific, operational language we can pass back to our counsel that would be helpful.

Appreciate it — Jane

[Acme ticket: ACME-INC-DPA-2027-041]

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodai.com>
To: Jane Alvarez <j.alvarez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident notification timing and cooperation language for DPA

Jane — thanks for the clear ask. High level response:

- We can commit to an initial notification within 48 hours of detection of a confirmed incident that materially affects customer data, with a statement of known scope and prioritised next steps.
- Because investigations evolve, we'll follow up with detailed incident reports on a defined cadence: initial notice (48h), interim update (72h), and final report within 30 days (or sooner if remediation completes). If additional time is required for complex forensic work, we'll notify and propose a revised timeline.
- "Reasonable cooperation" from Redwood: provide an assigned security POC, provide sanitized telemetry and relevant logs (subject to retention policy and legal constraints), participate in joint incident calls during the investigation window, and share remediation recommendations. We cannot provide production-level credentials or direct write access to customer environments.

I'm looping in Neha (privacy) and Laura (customer success) to confirm the operational bits and attach a draft playbook and suggested DPA redlines.

Thanks — Steph

[Attachment: incident_response_playbook_v2.pdf]

Internal thread — notes and suggested edits:

Stephanie — this is a good baseline. A few items legal will likely push back on and we should pre-empt:

1) 48 hours vs 72 hours: 48 hours for "initial notification" is industry-acceptable, but we should qualify it as "within 48 hours of confirmation of a security incident materially affecting customer data." That avoids a premature 48-hour timer based on noisy alerts.

2) Evidence access: propose "provision of relevant logs and sanitized artifacts" with an explicit statement that disclosure is subject to Redwood's data minimization and third-party privacy obligations. Call out that if Acme requires unredacted data for regulatory purposes, they must provide a lawful basis and a signed data request (and Redwood may require a separate engagement).

3) Preservation window: we should include a preservation period for retention of forensic artifacts (e.g., 90 days) and an option to extend on written request.

4) Communications: suggest Redwood owns customer-facing messaging draft, with Acme allowed to co-brand and request changes within 24 hours.

I'll draft redline language for each point and attach a playbook excerpt.

Neha

Subject: Re: Incident notification timing and cooperation language for DPA

Jane — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal ops and legal input together. Attached are: (1) a concise incident-notification playbook excerpt that maps timelines to deliverables, and (2) a redline DPA showing the proposed language. High-level summary below and the proposed draft language appended to this message.

Summary (proposed):
- Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial notification within 48 hours of confirmation of a security incident that materially affects Acme customer data. The initial notice will include a summary of known affected assets and an initial assessment of impact.
- Interim updates: Redwood will provide an interim update within 72 hours of the initial notice and thereafter at least every 72 hours until containment or a mutually agreed-upon cadence.
- Final report: Redwood will deliver a final report within 30 days of containment that includes root cause analysis, remediation steps, and lessons learned.
- Cooperation scope: Redwood will assign a security POC, provide non-sensitive telemetry and relevant logs subject to data minimization, participate in joint incident calls, and provide draft customer-facing messaging. Redwood will not provide production write access to customer environments and will require formal, scoped requests for any additional data that could implicate third-party privacy obligations.
- Preservation and evidence: Redwood will preserve relevant forensic artifacts for 90 days and agrees to consider extensions on written request. Evidence delivery mechanisms are secure-share/SFTP; any extended forensic exports are scopeable and billable.

Proposed redline snippet for the DPA (plain text for review):
"Redwood will provide an initial notification to Customer within forty-eight (48) hours of confirmation of a Security Incident materially affecting Customer Data. Such initial notification shall include the date/time of detection, summary of affected systems and data categories, and initial mitigation steps. Redwood shall provide interim updates within seventy-two (72) hours following the initial notification and thereafter at least every seventy-two (72) hours until containment. A final incident report, including root cause analysis and remediation summary, will be provided within thirty (30) days of containment, subject to extension where necessary for complex forensic work upon prior written notice to Customer.

Redwood's cooperation obligations shall include: (a) assignment of a security point of contact for the incident; (b) provision of non-sensitive telemetry and relevant logs, where permissible under Redwood's data retention and third-party obligations; (c) participation in joint incident calls and reasonable assistance in Customer communications; and (d) preservation of forensic artifacts for a period of ninety (90) days with the option to extend upon written request. Customer acknowledges that Redwood will not grant production-level credentials or write access to Customer systems as part of routine cooperation and that requests for expanded access or unredacted data must be separately scoped and agreed in writing."

Next steps: please review the attached redline and playbook excerpt. If that language is broadly acceptable, we can incorporate minor edits and circulate to your counsel for formal sign-off. If Acme prefers alternate timelines (e.g., 24h initial notice) flag that and we can evaluate operationally but we expect that will be limited to high-severity regulatory incidents.

Attachments: redline_DPA_20270411.docx; incident_response_playbook_v2.pdf; SOC2_summary_2026.pdf

Thanks — Steph
